title: Campilot shell
brief: Redesign the Campilot (Rust + egui CAM app) desktop shell after the visual and structural concept extracted from the reference app Prancheta CNC: one line-weight icon language, a graphite canvas that outranks the panels, a 200 px rail of five labelled groups that folds, a right panel that is a ribbon plus the task it opens, two millimetre rulers, a status bar in three zones, and teaching strings inside the tool. There is no stage bar: the workflow is carried by the rail and by whatever task the panel has open.

artboards.title: 2D shell — app bar, a 200 px rail of five labelled groups, two rulers, ribbon plus the open task, three-zone status bar
artboards.tradeoff: One screen, one job: every command is reachable by folding a group instead of remembering a mode, but twenty-eight glyph-only chips put the teaching burden on tooltips and on the status bar sentence that answers each press.

artboards.title: Where the workflow went, once the stage bar was removed
artboards.tradeoff: The workflow lives in the rail and in the task the panel has open, so nothing has to be remembered as a place you are standing; the cost is that progress is legible only from the document and from the status bar, never from a strip that totals it up.

artboards.title: Icon set — 71 glyphs on one 24 × 24 grid
artboards.tradeoff: A single stroke weight reads as one hand and never shimmers when selection moves; the cost is that no icon can carry fine detail, so complex strategies rely on tooltips and on labels the rail does not draw.

artboards.title: Visual tokens — dark and light, two signals, type and geometry
artboards.tradeoff: Two signal colours keep cut and selection unambiguous in monochrome and for colour-blind operators; the cost is a monochrome UI whose personality has to be carried by icon quality and by one 13 % wash.
